thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for /v1/generate (us-west) — error rate spike at 21:00 UTC. Paging on-call.
alex: oncall here, seeing spike in 5xx + backend timeouts. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/batching?from=now-15m
maria: I see large queue depth on batcher-service-*, latency tail skyrocketed. Likely head-of-line blocking in scheduler.
li: logs show continuous 'batcher: enqueue_time exceeded threshold' and repeated `evict_attempt` in runtime logs.
sam: stack traces show scheduler stuck trying to assemble huge batch (>512 tokens), then KV cache lookups timing out.
james: customer impact: a subset of requests are timing out at gateway (504) and some upstream 502s. Support already fielding multiple P1s.
ops: Can we triage traffic? Suggest immediate mitigation: disable automatic batching for high-concurrency route and route to small fixed-size batches.
alex: doing a quick canary — setting route config for /v1/generate to batching.enabled=false for us-west-1 traffic (will flip in console now).
incident-bot: deploy triggered by alex (config-change). CI job: config-apply-2143654800. Rollout in progress.
maria: while that rolls out, we should increase scheduler worker count to drain backlog: kubectl scale deploy/batcher-scheduler --replicas=6 -n inference
li: I can scale up nodes but need approval for burst GPU allocation; request sent to infra-alloc team.
sam: alternative: enable preemptive eviction policy to evict oldest waiting requests (runbook: /runbooks/batcher-hol.md). Command:
```
POST /admin/evict?policy=oldest
```
james: please note eviction will cause some customer requests to fail — need to notify support & customers.
ops: support message drafted: "We’re seeing intermittent timeouts for generation requests in us-west. Engineers are mitigating; retrying should succeed. Goal: restore within 15-30m." Send once mitigation applied.
li: infra approved burst nodes for 30m. Spinning up two g4dn pools.
alex: config change rolled out to 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 2m. Observing slight drop in 5xx but queue still high.
maria: scaling scheduler from 2->6 helped throughput but latency p95 still high; looks like head-of-line because big requests block smaller ones.
sam: temp workaround: enable small-batch route (max_batch_size=8) for urgent traffic and add route header x-priority=high to route treatment. Will add header at gateway for small requests.
incident-bot: checkpoint: 21:07 UTC — batching disabled for /v1/generate, eviction policy enabled, scheduler scaled. Monitoring for error rate and tail latency.
alex: metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 4% in 5m. Gateway 504s still at ~2%. Queue depth trending down slowly.
james: Support updated customers and opened follow-ups for any failed requests. PR for retry-window explanation posted in support docs.
ops: please capture relevant logs and timeline for postmortem. Tagging @pager to create incident CR.
pager: incident created: INC-2143654800. Severity: Sev2. Initial impact: degraded availability for generation endpoints in us-west; estimated affected %: 8-12% of requests.
maria: action items: 1) postmortem capture (owner: maria) 2) investigate why large batches not throttled upstream (owner: sam) 3) add circuit breaker on batch build time (owner: li) 4) improve runbook for rapid eviction (owner: alex).
li: I’ll open infra ticket to add ephemeral capacity automation for sudden batcher saturation.
sam: root-cause hypothesis: unbounded client that started sending long sequence requests without backpressure -> scheduler attempts to form huge batches -> head-of-line blocks short requests -> timeouts cascade. Need request-size enforcement at gateway.
alex: next steps: keep monitoring for 30m, keep support updated, proceed with documented remediation tasks. If error rate goes above 5% again, escalate to Sev1.
ops: thanks all. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. :white_check_mark:
